content: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood (TEC) is a condition that develops gradually in early childhood and is characterized by anemia, which manifests as a pale appearance in affected children. The exact cause of TEC remains unknown, but there is evidence to suggest that infection with Parvovirus B19 may play a role in its development. Children with TEC typically present with symptoms at a median age of 18 to 26 months. However, the condition can also occur in infants as young as 6 months or in older children up to 10 years of age. Due to the slow progression of anemia in TEC, affected children often appear healthier than one might expect given their significantly low hemoglobin levels. Most children with TEC recover fully within one to two months without long-term complications.
